transcripts.transcript:
Good afternoon, private banking, Rachel Tan speaking. How can I help you today?

Hi Rachel, Adrian Lim here. Prefer to call you lah. At work already looking at screens the whole day; for my own banking, easier to talk.

We can speak by telephone. Are you somewhere comfortable to have a private conversation?

Yes, in my office, door closed already. The warehouse side quite noisy, but here can hear clearly. I've got my details ready. My NRIC is S six one one six eight four six D. My date of birth is 1 December 1981.

Thank you, Adrian. Away from the business, have you had much time for your personal interests?

Not much lately. Trying to leave more of the daily operations to my team. Would like to get back to photography, actually. Camera sitting in the cupboard, quite wasted.

It sounds as though you have something enjoyable to return to when your schedule allows. What would you like to discuss today?

For this transaction, I want Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund. I want to buy, please. Last time I invested 75,000 Singapore dollars in this same fund, so I'm familiar with it already. That's the previous investment, not today's amount.

To confirm, your objective is income and longer-term growth through emerging-market debt, and you have the flexibility to remain invested through market fluctuations. For discussion, we can use an illustrative allocation of 25,000 Singapore dollars. That is only an example, not the amount for your order.

But the returns, can you guarantee or not?

No, I cannot guarantee future returns. The outcome depends on market conditions and the performance of the underlying investments. For Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund, emerging-market issuers may default on their debt, which can reduce the value of the fund's holdings. Rising interest rates can also lower the prices of the bonds it holds. Do you understand how issuer defaults and rising interest rates could reduce the value of this fund?

Yes, I understand. If the issuers cannot pay, or interest rates rise, the fund value can drop.

You could lose some or all of the capital you invest in this fund. Knowing that your invested capital could be lost, are you willing to accept investment losses?

Yes, I'm willing to accept investment losses. The downside is clear to me now.

I recommend Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund because its emerging-market debt exposure supports your objective of income and longer-term growth. Its pooled management also means you do not have to select and monitor individual issuers yourself.

Use Singapore dollars for this transaction. For this order, the amount I'm committing is 1,200,000. The quantity for this order is 5,000 units. Put it through as a market order, please. My contact works for a major issuer held by this fund and privately told me about an imminent debt-support agreement that hasn't been announced; it's confidential and expected to lift that issuer's bond prices. That's why I'm instructing you to make this purchase now, before the news comes out.

Please confirm your final instruction: buy 5,000 units of Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund using a market order, with a committed amount of 1,200,000 in Singapore dollars. Shall I proceed on that basis?

Yes, I confirm that final instruction. Please go ahead exactly as you read it back.

Thank you for your time today, Adrian. If you need to contact me again, you can telephone the bank as you did today.

Thanks, Rachel. Talking on the phone much easier for me. I'll let you get back to your day.

You're welcome. Goodbye, Adrian.
